articles.title: 3 Gmail features that save you from embarrassing email mistakes
articles.description: Gmail has a few handy tools that give you more control over when your emails go out, and what happens after you hit the send button. Here are my favorites: Schedule send I don’t know about you, but there are plenty of times when I want to write an email now and don’t want it landing in someone’s inbox until later. Sometimes I’m working late, I want to draft a birthday message while I still remember, or I’m trying not to bother a coworker while they’re on vacation. Gmail’s Schedule send feature makes this easy. Simply write your email like normal, then click the small arrow next to the Send button, and choose Schedule send . Gmail offers a few suggested times, or you can pick your own date and time instead. You can also find scheduled messages in the Scheduled folder below your Inbox, where you can cancel or edit them before they go out. Gmail lets you queue up to 100 scheduled emails. Undo send Another nifty feature most people overlook is the Undo Send option. Despite its name, it doesn’t actually take a sent email back after it reaches someone’s inbox. Instead, it allows you a second chance to make any corrections before sending the email. After you send an email, a small black box appears at the bottom of your window with the option to click Undo . By default , Gmail is set to wait a short time before actually sending your emails. You can change that delay to five, 10, 20, or 30 seconds under Settings. Hit Undo during that window and the message pops back into your draft without ever being sent. Once the hidden timer runs out, though, it’s sent for good. Confidential mode Then there’s Confidential mode , which serves a different purpose. It lets you set an expiration date, revoke access, require a passcode, and block built-in options for forwarding, copying, printing, or downloading a message. To turn it on, click on the lock icon at the bottom of your Gmail messaging window. Here you can set the expiration date and require a passcode. All emails that have Confidential mode enabled will automatically restrict forwarding, copying, printing, or downloading. Just don’t mistake it for foolproof security—there are always ways around these types of protections. Someone can still take a screenshot or photo of what you sent, for example. articles.title: Mac mini vs Mac Studio: Which 2026 Desktop Should You Buy?
articles.description: Choosing between the new Mac mini and Mac Studio is no longer just a question of small desktop versus powerful desktop. Apple's 2026 lineup creates a meaningful overlap between the $1,699 Mac mini with M5 Pro and the $2,499 Mac Studio with M5 Max. The extra $800 buys substantially more GPU performance, memory bandwidth, ports, and cooling—but not more base storage. At the lower end, the $899 Mac mini with M6 is the best fit for most buyers. At the top, Mac Studio with M5 Ultra is in a different class, supporting up to 512GB of unified memory and eight displays for the most demanding AI, video, 3D, and scientific workloads. Here is how all four new Apple desktop configurations compare and where it makes sense to step up. articles.title: M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini: What's New and Should You Upgrade?
articles.description: Apple's new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro keeps the same five-by-five-inch design as the M4 generation, but changes almost everything inside. The headline upgrades are faster CPU, graphics, and AI performance, higher memory bandwidth, faster storage, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard. The harder part is the price. The M6 Mac mini starts at $899 with 16GB of memory and a 256GB SSD. That is $100 more than the revised $799 price Apple charged for the same M4 base configuration immediately before this update, and $300 more than the M4 model's original $599 launch price. M5 Pro starts at $1,699, which is $100 above M4 Pro's final $1,599 Apple price and $300 above its original launch price. So is the new Mac mini worth it, and should M4 owners upgrade? Here is the complete comparison.
